home.stepsHeading: How to Merge Audio Files Online in 3 Steps
home.stepsIntro: Our free online audio joiner works entirely inside your browser using the Web Audio API, so you can combine audio files in seconds without creating an account or waiting on slow server uploads.
home.step1Body: Click Add files or drag and drop MP3, WAV, OGG, M4A, AAC, or FLAC files directly onto the studio canvas. Join multiple audio tracks into one list and reorder them freely.
home.step2Body: Click any track to open its interactive waveform. Drag the left and right trim handles—or type exact Start and End timestamps—and toggle the 3-second equal-power crossfade between adjacent songs.
home.step3Body: Choose MP3 (192 kbps) or lossless 16-bit PCM WAV, then press Join. A dedicated background Web Worker encodes your merged track while keeping the interface smooth and responsive.
home.easyBody: Whether you need an MP3 joiner online for a quick mashup or want to stitch audio files together for a presentation, the focal workspace keeps every essential control within immediate reach—without cluttered toolbars.
home.unlimitedBody: Combine WAV and MP3 files in the same timeline, or mix OGG, M4A, and FLAC tracks together. Our client-side audio merger resamples every clip automatically to a unified 44.1 kHz stereo output with no artificial track count cap.
home.crossfadeBody: Eliminate abrupt cuts when you combine songs online. Enabling crossfade applies a smooth 3-second equal-power curve so one track gently fades out while the next fades in at consistent acoustic volume.
home.privacyTitle: Private Browser Audio Joiner — Zero Uploads
home.privacyBody: Unlike traditional tools that transfer your private recordings to remote servers, this no upload audio joiner processes 100% of your audio locally on your device. Because nothing travels over the network, there are no artificial server file-size caps—only your browser's own available memory.
home.useCasesHeading: Popular Ways to Combine Audio Files
home.useCasesIntro: Creators, musicians, students, and podcasters rely on a private client-side audio merger every day:
home.useCase1Body: Stitch intro music, guest interviews, sponsor reads, and outro segments together with clean trims and smooth transitions.
home.useCase2Body: Join voice memos from lectures, interviews, or meetings into a single continuous recording for easy sharing or archiving.
home.useCase3Body: Combine multiple chapter MP3 files or study tracks into one uninterrupted file for long commutes or offline players.
home.useCase4Body: Trim favorite choruses, crossfade beats together, and export a custom ringtone or continuous workout playlist in MP3 or WAV.
home.faq1Q: Is this online audio joiner really free and unlimited?
home.faq1A: Yes. Audio Joiner is completely free with no watermarks, sign-ups, or artificial track limits. Since all decoding and joining runs inside your own browser, you can combine as many tracks as your device memory comfortably handles.
home.faq2Q: Are my audio files uploaded to any server?
home.faq2A: Never. Every file is decoded locally via your browser's Web Audio API and encoded in a local Web Worker. Your songs, voice recordings, and private clips never leave your computer or phone.
home.faq3Q: Which audio formats can I combine together?
home.faq3A: You can mix and merge MP3, WAV, OGG, M4A, AAC, and FLAC files in the same timeline, and export the final joined track as either 192 kbps MP3 or lossless 16-bit PCM WAV.
home.faq4Q: How does the 3-second crossfade feature work?
home.faq4A: When Crossfade is enabled on a track, Audio Joiner overlaps the final 3 seconds of that clip with the first 3 seconds of the next clip using an equal-power sine/cosine curve so the volume stays balanced with no sudden dip.
home.faq5Q: Can I trim individual tracks before joining them?
home.faq5A: Yes. Expand any track in the stack and drag the left or right trim handles on the waveform, or enter exact timestamps in the Start and End fields at the bottom.
home.faq6Q: Does Audio Joiner work on mobile phones and tablets?
home.faq6A: Yes. The responsive workspace works on desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers with touch-friendly waveform trim handles and a streamlined icons-only navigation bar on smaller screens.

howTo.subtitle: A practical guide to trimming, crossfading, and merging audio files privately inside your browser.
howTo.s1Body: Open the Audio Joiner homepage and click Add files (or drag files directly onto the studio box). You can add MP3, WAV, OGG, M4A, AAC, or FLAC files—even mixed formats in the same project. Use the floating Up and Down buttons beside an expanded track to change playback order, or Delete to remove a clip.
howTo.s2Body: Click any numbered track row to expand its waveform canvas. Drag the light aqua Start and End handles inward to remove silence, coughs, or unwanted intros. For frame-accurate edits, type exact times directly into the Start and End boxes in the bottom transport bar—both controls stay synced in real time.
howTo.s3Body: To blend two songs or podcast segments together smoothly, expand the earlier track and click the Crossfade icon in the top-right corner. Audio Joiner applies a 3-second equal-power crossfade overlap (automatically scaled down if a clip is shorter than 7 seconds) and updates your merged timeline duration live.
howTo.s4Body: Press Play in the bottom bar (or click anywhere on an expanded waveform) to audition your joined timeline with crossfades applied. Choose MP3 (compact 192 kbps stereo) for sharing and podcasts, or WAV (lossless 16-bit PCM) for studio editing, then click Join to encode and download locally.
howTo.tip1: Use WAV export if you plan to bring the merged file into a video editor or DAW for further mastering.
howTo.tip2: Combine voice memos recorded on iPhone (M4A) and Android or desktop (MP3/WAV) in one unified timeline without converting them first.
howTo.tip3: Leave Crossfade off for spoken-word voice notes or strict chapter breaks, and turn it on for music mixes and intros.
howTo.tip4: Click directly on any expanded waveform during playback to jump straight to that moment in the joined sequence.
howTo.privacyBoxBody: Everything runs offline-capable inside your browser tab via AudioContext, OfflineAudioContext, and a dedicated Web Worker. Zero files are ever uploaded, stored, or inspected on external servers.
